post.summary: Send a message in a conversation and get Claude's response
post.description: Returns the whole turn as one JSON response. The web UI sends turns through the streaming variant (POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages/stream, server-sent events) and falls back to this endpoint when a stream cannot be opened, e.g. behind a reverse proxy that buffers text/event-stream. This endpoint is supported and suits scripts and API clients that want a single response rather than an event stream.

post.summary: Start a manual run over files and folders
post.description: Checks that every id is readable by the user and queues the run; the work starts on the next background-job tick. Folders are walked recursively unless `options.recursive` is false. Files picked one by one are always processed; files found in a folder are skipped when their output is already up to date, unless `options.force` is true. Outputs go beside each source, or into `options.outputFolder`.

options.description: Shared options (`recursive`, `force`, `outputFolder`, `maxBytesPerFile`, `mimeTypes`) plus the operation's own (`style` for summarize, `targetLanguage` for translate)

mode.description: `batch` (half price, up to 24 hours) or `immediate` (full price); defaults to `batch` when the provider supports it

folderIds.description: Folders whose text documents to process

400.description: Invalid input, or more ids than a run takes (`limit` names the cap)

429.description: Too many runs started in the last hour (`limit` names the cap)

404.description: A file or folder is not found or not readable

401.description: Current user is not logged in

get.summary: Get one manual run, with its log
get.description: `pollIntervalSeconds` suggests when to ask again; it is null once the run has ended. `outputs` lists the files written, as paths in the user's Files. Log entries are oldest first, at most the newest 500.

parameters.name: id

post.summary: Cancel a manual run

tags.name: page
tags.description: Page Controller for AIquila main interface

tags.name: stream_probe
tags.description: A miniature Server-Sent Events endpoint whose only job is to be measured. The chat stream cannot double as a diagnostic: it needs a configured provider, a conversation and an LLM round trip, and it bills the account. This one emits a few empty ticks a fixed interval apart, so the StreamingNotBuffered setup check can tell whether something between PHP and the client is holding the response back — the failure that turns streaming chat into a long wait followed by the whole reply at once. It is a public page because the setup check requests it over the loopback without a session. It reveals nothing: the payload is a tick index and a server timestamp.

tags.name: project_template
tags.description: Project templates: the title, description, system prompt and path suggestions a new project is copied from. A project made from a template is a copy. Editing or deleting the template later leaves it alone. `/api/project-templates` holds the caller's own templates and lists the instance ones; `/api/admin/project-templates` is where admins publish instance templates.

tags.name: prompt
tags.description: The prompt library: reusable snippets a user inserts into a message or a project's system prompt. `/api/prompts` manages the caller's own prompts and lists the instance ones read-only. `/api/admin/prompts` is the admin side, for instance prompts only; the framework refuses those routes to non-admins.

tags.name: sequence
tags.description: Sequences: named chains of MCP tool calls the AIquila MCP server runs in one call, as the calling user. `/api/sequences` manages the caller's own sequences, lists the organization's read-only, and switches built-ins on or off for the caller. `/api/sequences/effective` is what the MCP server reads, with an ETag. `/api/admin/sequences` and `/api/admin/sequence-policy` are the admin side; the framework refuses them to non-admins.

tags.name: instructions
tags.description: Instance instructions: admin text placed in front of the system prompt for every user, on the surfaces the admin enables. Admin-only; the framework refuses both routes to other users.

tags.name: provider_settings
tags.description: Schema-driven read/write of provider configuration for the settings pages. Both the admin and the personal page render whatever LLMProviderInterface::getSettingsSchema() describes, so this controller never names a provider or a config key — adding a provider requires no change here. The admin/user split is enforced twice over: the admin routes carry no #[NoAdminRequired] (so Nextcloud requires an admin), and ProviderSettingsService::writeUser() additionally drops any field whose scope is not user-writable. That second check is what keeps endpoint URLs — which decide where the server sends outbound requests — out of reach of the personal page even if a route were ever mis-annotated. Provider *access* is enforced on top of that: index() only describes providers the current user is permitted to use, and update() refuses one they are not, so the personal page can neither see nor select a provider an admin blocked.

tags.name: usage_export
tags.description: Downloads of the token usage in `aiquila_usage_stats`, as CSV or JSON. `/api/usage/export` is the caller's own usage and takes no user: there is no parameter through which a user could name anyone else. `/api/admin/usage/export` covers every user, or one user or group; the framework refuses it to non-admins with 403. The body streams (DownloadStreamResponse), so a year of per-request rows never sits in memory. Parameters are checked before the first byte; once streaming starts the status is 200.

tags.name: batch_run
tags.description: Manual batch runs: one operation over files and folders the user picked. Used by the "Process with AIquila…" action in Files and by the MCP server (app password, hence NoCSRFRequired alongside NoAdminRequired).

tags.name: coworker
tags.description: REST API for cowork tasks — persistent scheduled AI jobs. Consumed by the Cowork UI and by the MCP server (Basic Auth), hence NoCSRFRequired alongside NoAdminRequired.

tags.name: coworker_trigger
tags.description: The trigger URL of a coworker, for other systems: an orchestrator, a Webhook listeners webhook, a CI job. The caller has no Nextcloud session. It proves itself with the coworker's trigger secret as a bearer token (RFC 6750 §2.1, the header form only: a secret in the query string would end up in access logs). An unknown coworker and a wrong secret get the same 401, so the endpoint does not tell which coworker IDs exist, and both count as a brute-force attempt. The request body is not read. A trigger only says "run now"; what the run works on is the coworker's own input folder, so a caller cannot put text in front of the model or point the coworker at other files.
